problem: Existing online open-vocabulary 3D mapping systems segment every frame, associate each frame-local mask to the 3D map via voxel/rendered-view matching, and run vision-language inference frequently, which is costly in compute and GPU memory.
motivation: Robots need online, queryable object-level maps (scene graphs) for language-guided search on onboard hardware. Consecutive frames are highly redundant, so mask identity can be maintained cheaply in image space rather than solved as a 3D association problem for every frame.
key_idea: Track FastSAM mask identities between sparse keyframes in image space via DINOv3 dense feature label propagation, fuse the tracks into a TSDF/mesh to build class-agnostic 3D segments in a Hydra scene graph, and use 3D association only for interruptions and revisits.
insight: Short-term identity resolved in 2D gives comparable mapping quality at much higher throughput: replacing the tracker with per-frame FastSAM + BoT-SORT drops max rate from 15.0 to 6.0 Hz with near-identical AP (6.01 vs 6.00) and lower AP50/AP25/synonym frequency. Keeping separate per-track CLIP galleries with max-similarity scoring beats a mean feature (AP 6.00 vs 5.65, synonyms 0.50 vs 0.45). On HM3D, the weak AP/AP50 despite competitive AP25 suggests segments often under-cover the object extent in larger scenes.
method: Image-space tracker: FastSAM-x masks and CLIP features are computed every K_f=24 frames; DINOv3 ViT-S+ dense features run on every frame, and patch-level label propagation (softmax-weighted top-similarity reference patches from the keyframe and recent frames) carries source-track identities between keyframes.

Keyframe correction: each FastSAM mask is matched to propagated track masks with score 0.5*IoU + 0.5*DINOv3 cosine, under minimum thresholds and greedy one-to-one assignment; unmatched detections start new tracks, unmatched tracks are retired, and track DINOv3 features are updated with an EMA (eta=0.2).

Track fusion into TSDF/mesh: each voxel keeps up to K=4 source-track hypotheses with accumulated weights; propagated masks get confidence alpha/(1+beta*Δt), so their influence decays since the last keyframe; mesh vertices inherit the hypotheses.

3D segment updater: vertices are grouped by winning track; a new track is merged into an active segment if mesh-vertex overlap (either direction ≥0.75) and DINOv3 similarity (≥0.80) hold, otherwise a new segment node is created. This replaces Hydra's object layer with a class-agnostic segment layer.

Long-term re-identification: a k-d tree over centroids of historical segments retrieves candidates; the score combines geometric overlap (r_nn=0.10 m) and DINOv3 cosine, and accepted matches merge into the historical node and reactivate it.

CLIP galleries and querying: asynchronous CLIP on bbox crops is averaged per source track, and each segment stores one feature per track; the query score is the max cosine over the gallery, returning a ranked list of segments (text or image queries).

setting.backbone: FastSAM-x + OpenCLIP ViT-H/14 (ViT-L and ViT-B variants) + DINOv3 ViT-S+ (29M), all frozen pretrained
setting.observation: RGB-D + odometry (LiDAR-inertial odometry on the real robot)
setting.action_space: none for mapping; retrieved segment positions used as navigation goals for a quadruped, exploration via a volumetric planner
setting.simulator: Not a simulator: offline datasets Replica, ScanNet++, HM3D via OpenLex3D; real quadruped and recorded drone data

numbers.extra: processes every frame; Top-5 segmentation frequencies and retrieval AP

numbers_note: Not a navigation-success benchmark: OpenLex3D open-vocabulary segmentation/retrieval numbers (no official split names; 'val' used as placeholder). Real-world results are qualitative (all queried targets retrieved in 3 environments). Efficiency on Replica (Table 3): 8.9 min, 9.5 GB RAM, 8.3 GB VRAM at 3 cm (ViT-H); 3.9 min at 5 cm.
results: On OpenLex3D, TrackGraph has the highest synonym frequency on Replica (0.50), beating OVI-MAP SigLIP-L (0.49), and is second on ScanNet++ (0.35 vs HOV-SG 0.40). Retrieval trails OVI-MAP (SigLIP-L AP 10.49 on Replica) and is weak on HM3D AP. On the same A100 it is 1.7x faster and uses 3.3x less GPU memory than ViT-H OVI-MAP (8.3 vs 27.2 GB), and runs onboard a quadruped at 7.5 Hz.
limitations: Retrieval AP/AP50 is below OVI-MAP and other baselines on HM3D, where segments under-cover objects, likely because instance continuity is harder in large scenes.

Efficiency comparisons are not measured under identical hardware and frame settings (baselines are from an RTX 3090 and process every 10th frame), so they are only indicative; real-world results are qualitative.
Relies on given odometry, FastSAM mask quality, and hand-tuned thresholds.
